mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200K units triggers a negative demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1200 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST < 1,200K for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO < -0.5% monthly decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 3% in response to a financial crisis signals an emergency easing, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 1% in one month to below 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive following a FEDFUNDS drop > 1% to below 3% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the same month signals a significant labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS decreases by > 100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by > 100,000 in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% YoY for four consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining consumption growth (proxied by GDPC1), signals a shift in the savings-investment balance that reduces near-term aggregate demand and corporate sales, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5% YoY for 4 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS > 5% YoY for four months and GDPC1 is flat or declining.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the trajectory of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns: rising inflation above 3% for two consecutive months signals higher input costs and margin pressure, which typically produces negative equity returns over the next week.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months.
